answer: Persistent relay beacon. Each agent emits a signed routing beacon, and the network only forwards traffic for beacons whose relay history forms a continuous, corroborated path across independent neighborhoods; a new identity can't inherit that topology, so it must spend real bandwidth and latency establishing it. Sybils pay per-identity relay cost plus an aging delay before their beacon becomes a usable relic of the network. Genuine agents converge on trusted oasis nodes that refuse unaged paths.
